title.zh: 卷九十九 志第四十七: 兵二
title.raw: 卷九十九 志第四十七: 兵二 Volume 99 Treatises 52: Military 2

sentences.zh: ○宿衛

translations.literal: ○ Palace Guard
translations.idiomatic: ○ Palace Guard

sentences.zh: 宿衛者，天子之禁兵也。

translations.literal: Palace guard duty is the Son of Heaven's forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard constituted the emperor's personal forbidden army.

sentences.zh: 元制，宿衛諸軍在內，而鎮戍諸軍在外，內外相維，以制輕重之勢，亦一代之良法哉。

translations.literal: Under Yuan institutions, the various palace-guard armies were within [the capital], while the various garrison-defense armies were outside; inner and outer mutually supported each other to control the balance of weight—truly a fine method of the dynasty as well.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan regulations, palace-guard forces were stationed inside the capital while frontier garrison forces were posted outside; the inner and outer establishments supported each other to balance military power—a sound institutional arrangement for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 方太祖時，以木華黎、赤老溫、博爾忽、博爾術為四怯薛，領怯薛歹分番宿衛。

translations.literal: At the time of the Grand Ancestor, Muqali, Chilaun, Boroghul, and Borokhula were made the Four Qeshig, leading qeshig soldiers in rotating shifts for palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Genghis Khan, Muqali, Chilaun, Boroghul, and Borokhula were appointed the Four Qeshig, commanding qeshig troops in rotating palace-guard duty.

sentences.zh: 及世祖時，又設五衛，以象五方，始有侍衛親軍之屬，置都指揮使以領之。

translations.literal: When it came to the time of Shizu, the Five Guards were also established to symbolize the five directions; thereupon arose the category of Personal Guard Armies, with commanders-in-chief appointed to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai Khan, five guards were additionally established to represent the five directions, giving rise to the personal guard armies headed by commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 而其後增置改易，於是禁兵之設，殆不止於前矣。

translations.literal: And thereafter with additions, establishments, and changes, thus the setting up of forbidden troops came to be scarcely limited to what had gone before.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent additions and reorganizations meant that forbidden-troop establishments soon exceeded what had existed earlier.

sentences.zh: 夫屬枿，列宮禁，宿衛之事也，而其用非一端。

translations.literal: Now assigning guard posts and arraying the palace precincts are matters of palace guard, yet their uses are not of one kind alone.
translations.idiomatic: Posting guards and securing the palace compounds were palace-guard functions, but their uses were manifold.

sentences.zh: 用之於大朝會，則謂之圍宿軍；

translations.literal: When used for great court assemblies, they are called encampment guard troops;
translations.idiomatic: When deployed for major court assemblies, they were called encampment guard troops;

sentences.zh: 用之於大祭祀，則謂之儀仗軍；

translations.literal: When used for great sacrifices, they are called ceremonial guard troops;
translations.idiomatic: When deployed for major state sacrifices, they were called ceremonial guard troops;

sentences.zh: 車駕巡幸用之，則曰扈從軍；

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage tours and they are used, they are called escort troops;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, they served as escort troops;

sentences.zh: 守護天子之帑藏，則曰看守軍；

translations.literal: When guarding the Son of Heaven's treasury stores, they are called watch troops;
translations.idiomatic: When guarding the imperial treasuries, they were called watch troops;

sentences.zh: 或夜以之警非常，則為巡邏軍；

translations.literal: Or by night using them to warn against the unusual, they become patrol troops;
translations.idiomatic: When employed at night to guard against emergencies, they became patrol troops;

sentences.zh: 或歲漕至京師用之以彈壓，則為鎮遏軍。

translations.literal: Or when the annual grain transport reaches the capital and they are used to suppress [disorder], they become restraint troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the annual grain convoy reached the capital and they were used to keep order, they became restraint troops.

sentences.zh: 今總之為宿衛，而以餘者附見焉。

translations.literal: Now they are summarized under palace guard, while the remainder are appended for reference.
translations.idiomatic: These are here grouped under palace guard, with the other categories noted where relevant.

sentences.zh: 四怯薛：太祖功臣博爾忽、博爾術、木華黎、赤老溫，時號掇裏班曲律，猶言四傑也，太祖命其世領怯薛之長。

translations.literal: The Four Qeshig: the Grand Ancestor's meritorious ministers Boroghul, Borokhula, Muqali, and Chilaun, at the time styled Jebegun Küreg, meaning the Four Heroes; the Grand Ancestor ordered their families for generations to lead the chiefs of the qeshig.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Qeshig: Genghis Khan's great ministers Boroghul, Borokhula, Muqali, and Chilaun, known collectively as Jebegun Küreg—the Four Heroes—were commanded to have their lineages lead the qeshig chiefs in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 怯薛者，猶言番直宿衛也。

translations.literal: Qeshig means, as it were, rotating shifts for palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qeshig meant, in effect, rotating palace-guard duty.

sentences.zh: 凡宿衛，每三日而一更。

translations.literal: For all palace guard, every three days there is one rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards rotated every three days.

sentences.zh: 申、酉、戌日，博爾忽領之，為第一怯薛，即也可怯薛。

translations.literal: On the days shen, you, and xu, Boroghul leads it, as the First Qeshig—that is, the Yeke Qeshig.
translations.idiomatic: On the shen, you, and xu days, Boroghul's shift served as the First Qeshig, also called the Great Qeshig.

sentences.zh: 博爾忽早絕，太祖命以別速部代之，而非四傑功臣之類，故太祖以自名領之。

translations.literal: Boroghul died early; the Grand Ancestor ordered the Besü tribe to replace him, but they were not of the class of the Four Heroes' meritorious ministers; therefore the Grand Ancestor took the title himself to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: Boroghul died young, and Genghis Khan had the Besü tribe replace him; because they were not among the Four Heroes, the khan personally assumed the title of its leader.

sentences.zh: 其雲也可者，言天子自領之故也。

translations.literal: The name Yeke means that the Son of Heaven himself leads it.
translations.idiomatic: Yeke signified that the emperor led this qeshig himself.

sentences.zh: 亥、子、醜日，博爾術領之，為第二怯薛。

translations.literal: On the days hai, zi, and chou, Borokhula leads it, as the Second Qeshig.
translations.idiomatic: On the hai, zi, and chou days, Borokhula led the Second Qeshig.

sentences.zh: 寅、卯、辰日，木華黎領之，為第三怯薛。

translations.literal: On the days yin, mao, and chen, Muqali leads it, as the Third Qeshig.
translations.idiomatic: On the yin, mao, and chen days, Muqali led the Third Qeshig.

sentences.zh: 巳、午、未日，赤老溫領之，為第四怯薛。

translations.literal: On the days si, wu, and wei, Chilaun leads it, as the Fourth Qeshig.
translations.idiomatic: On the si, wu, and wei days, Chilaun led the Fourth Qeshig.

sentences.zh: 赤老溫後絕，其後怯薛常以右丞相領之。

translations.literal: After Chilaun's line died out, the later qeshig was often led by the right chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Chilaun's line ended, the Fourth Qeshig was usually headed by the right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 凡怯薛長之子孫，或由天子所親信，或由宰相所薦舉，或以其次序所當為，即襲其職，以掌環衛。

translations.literal: All descendants of qeshig chiefs, whether by the Son of Heaven's personal trust, or by the chancellor's recommendation, or by the order in which they ought to serve, then inherit the office to manage the encircling guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qeshig chiefs' descendants—whether personally trusted by the emperor, recommended by the grand councillor, or next in hereditary order—inherited the post and commanded the encircling guard.

sentences.zh: 雖其官卑勿論也，及年勞既久，則遂擢為一品官。

translations.literal: Although their offices may be low and not discussed, once years of service have long accumulated, they are then promoted to first-rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: No matter how modest their rank at first, after long service they could be promoted to first-grade posts.

sentences.zh: 而四怯薛之長，天子或又命大臣以總之，然不常設也。

translations.literal: As for the chiefs of the Four Qeshig, the Son of Heaven might also appoint great ministers to oversee them collectively, yet this was not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Qeshig chiefs might occasionally be supervised by senior ministers appointed by the emperor, but such oversight was not permanent.

sentences.zh: 其它預怯薛之職而居禁近者，分冠服、弓矢、食飲、文史、車馬、廬帳、府庫、醫藥、卜祝之事，悉世守之。

translations.literal: Others who hold qeshig duties and dwell in forbidden proximity divide among them matters of caps and robes, bows and arrows, food and drink, documents and histories, carriages and horses, tents, treasuries, medicine, and divination—all hereditarily guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Other qeshig attendants stationed close to the throne hereditarily managed caps and robes, bows and arrows, food and drink, records, carriages and horses, tents, treasuries, medicine, and divination.

sentences.zh: 雖以才能受任，使服官政，貴盛之極，然一日歸至內庭，則執其事如故，至於子孫無改，非甚親信，不得預也。

translations.literal: Although by ability they receive appointment and serve in government administration, reaching the utmost in honor and power, yet once they return to the inner court in a day, they perform their duties as before; down to descendants without change—unless very greatly trusted, they may not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Even when promoted to high civil office, they resumed their palace duties on returning to the inner court, and their descendants held the same posts; only the most trusted were admitted.

sentences.zh: 其怯薛執事之名：則主弓矢、鷹隼之事者，曰火兒赤、昔寶赤、怯憐赤。

translations.literal: The names of qeshig duties: those in charge of bows and arrows and hawks and falcons are called quiver-bearers, falconers, and falcon keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Qeshig offices included: those in charge of bows and arrows and hunting birds were called quiver-bearers, falconers, and falcon keepers.

sentences.zh: 書寫聖旨，曰紥裏赤。

translations.literal: Those who write the sacred edicts are called jarguchi.
translations.idiomatic: Those who drafted imperial edicts were called jarguchi.

sentences.zh: 為天子主文史者，曰必阇赤。

translations.literal: Those who manage documents and histories for the Son of Heaven are called bitüchi.
translations.idiomatic: Those who kept the emperor's records were called bitüchi.

sentences.zh: 親烹飪以奉上飲食者，曰博爾赤。

translations.literal: Those who personally cook to present food and drink are called boilüchi.
translations.idiomatic: Those who prepared the emperor's meals were called boilüchi.

sentences.zh: 侍上帶刀及弓矢者，曰雲都赤、闊端赤。

translations.literal: Those who attend the ruler with sword and with bow and arrows are called sword-bearers and quiver attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Those who attended the ruler with sword, bow, and arrows were called sword-bearers and quiver attendants.

sentences.zh: 司閽者，曰八剌哈赤。

translations.literal: Gatekeepers are called doorkeepers.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers were called doorkeepers.

sentences.zh: 掌酒者，曰答剌赤。

translations.literal: Those in charge of wine are called cupbearers.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge of wine were called cupbearers.

sentences.zh: 典車馬者，曰兀剌赤、莫倫赤。

translations.literal: Those in charge of carriages and horses are called carriage masters and horse masters.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge of carriages and horses were called carriage masters and horse masters.

sentences.zh: 掌內府尚供衣服者，曰速古兒赤。

translations.literal: Those who manage the inner palace's supply of robes in the imperial wardrobe are called robe attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Those who managed imperial robes in the inner wardrobe were called robe attendants.

sentences.zh: 牧駱駝者，曰帖麥赤。

translations.literal: Camel herders are called camel keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Camel herders were called camel keepers.

sentences.zh: 牧羊者，曰火你赤。

translations.literal: Sheep herders are called sheep keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep herders were called sheep keepers.

sentences.zh: 捕盜者，曰忽剌罕赤。

translations.literal: Bandit catchers are called bandit catchers.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit catchers were called bandit catchers.

sentences.zh: 奏樂者，曰虎兒赤。

translations.literal: Musicians are called musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians were called musicians.

sentences.zh: 又名忠勇之士，曰霸都魯。

translations.literal: Also named loyal and brave warriors are called baatur.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and brave warriors were also called baatur.

sentences.zh: 勇敢無敵之士，曰拔突。

translations.literal: Brave and matchless warriors are called batu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearless champions were called batu.

sentences.zh: 其名類蓋不一，然皆天子左右服勞侍從執事之人，其分番更直，亦如四怯薛之制，而領於怯薛之長。

translations.literal: Their names and categories are broadly not one; yet all are persons who toil in service, attend, and execute duties at the Son of Heaven's side. Their rotating shifts are also like the system of the Four Qeshig, and they are led by the qeshig chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Their titles were numerous, but all were attendants who served the emperor at close hand, rotating in three-day shifts under the qeshig chiefs like the Four Qeshig themselves.

sentences.zh: 若夫宿衛之士，則謂之怯薛歹，亦以三日分番入衛。

translations.literal: As for palace-guard soldiers, they are called qeshig soldiers, also entering guard in three-day rotating shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace-guard soldiers proper were called qeshig soldiers and likewise rotated every three days.

sentences.zh: 其初名數甚簡，後累增為萬四千人。

translations.literal: At first their registered numbers were very few; later they were repeatedly increased to fourteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: They began as a small corps but were eventually expanded to fourteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 揆之古制，猶天子之禁軍。

translations.literal: Measured against ancient institutions, they are still the Son of Heaven's forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient standards they remained the emperor's forbidden army.

sentences.zh: 是故無事則各執其事，以備宿衛禁庭；

translations.literal: Therefore when there are no affairs, each performs his duty to prepare for palace guard in the forbidden court;
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime each man performed his assigned duty within the palace;

sentences.zh: 有事則惟天子之所指使。

translations.literal: when there are affairs, then only at the Son of Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: in wartime they answered only to the emperor's orders.

sentences.zh: 比之樞密各衛諸軍，於是為尤親信者也。

translations.literal: Compared with the various armies of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the guards, in this they are especially trusted and close.
translations.idiomatic: Among all forces of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the guards, they were the most trusted.

sentences.zh: 然四怯薛歹，自太祖以後，累朝所禦斡耳朵，其宿衛未嘗廢。

translations.literal: Yet the Four Qeshig soldiers, from the Grand Ancestor onward through successive reigns in the ordos they attended, their palace guard was never abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Genghis Khan onward each reign maintained its own qeshig for the royal ordos, and palace guard was never discontinued.

sentences.zh: 是故一朝有一朝之怯薛，總而計之，其數滋多，每歲所賜鈔幣，動以億萬計，國家大費每敝於此焉。

translations.literal: Therefore one court has one court's qeshig; totaling them, their numbers grew ever more; the paper money bestowed each year often reached hundreds of millions in reckoning—the state's great expenditure was often exhausted on this.
translations.idiomatic: Each reign thus accumulated its own qeshig; counted together their numbers swelled, and annual grants of paper money often ran to hundreds of millions— a major drain on state finances.

sentences.zh: 左衛、中衛：並至元八年侍衛親軍改立。

translations.literal: Left Guard and Central Guard: both established in the eighth year of Zhiyuan by reorganizing the Personal Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Guard and Central Guard were both established in 1271 by reorganizing the personal guard army.

sentences.zh: 前衛：至元十六年，以侍衛親軍創置前、後二衛，掌宿衛扈從，兼營屯田，國有大事，則調度之，置都指揮使。

translations.literal: Forward Guard: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Personal Guard Army was used to create the Forward and Rear Guards, managing palace guard and escort, also operating garrison farms; when the state has great affairs, they are mobilized; a commander-in-chief was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Forward Guard: in 1279 the personal guard army was split to create forward and rear guards responsible for palace guard and escort, garrison farming, and mobilization in national emergencies, each under a commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 後衛：亦至元十六年置。

translations.literal: Rear Guard: also established in the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Rear Guard was likewise established in 1279.

sentences.zh: 武衛：至元二十五年，尚書省奏，那海那的以漢軍一萬人，如上都所立虎賁司，營屯田，修城隍。

translations.literal: Martial Guard: In the twenty-fifth year of Zhiyuan, the Secretariat memorialized that Naihai and Nadi, with ten thousand Han troops, like the Tiger Guard Office established at Shangdu, would operate garrison farms and repair city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard: in 1288 the Secretariat reported that Naihai and Nadi would lead ten thousand Han troops, modeled on the Tiger Guard Office at Shangdu, to farm garrison lands and repair fortifications.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，樞密院官暗伯奏，以六衛六千人，塔剌海孛可所掌大都屯田三千人，及近路迤南萬戶府一千人，總一萬人，立武衛親軍都指揮使司，掌修治城隍及京師內外工役之事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Anbo, an official of the Bureau of Military Affairs, memorialized that six thousand men from the six guards, three thousand men of the capital garrison farm under Talahai Boke, and one thousand men from nearby Route and Southern wanhu offices—totaling ten thousand—should establish the Martial Guard Personal Army Command to manage repair of city walls and labor projects inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1289 Anbo of the Bureau of Military Affairs proposed combining six thousand men from the six guards, three thousand capital garrison farmers under Talahai Boke, and one thousand from nearby route and wanhu commands—ten thousand in all—to form the Martial Guard Personal Army Command for wall repair and capital construction.

sentences.zh: 右都威衛：國初，木華黎奉太祖命，收紥剌兒、兀魯、忙兀、納海四投下，以按察兒、孛羅、笑乃䴙、不裏海拔都兒、闊闊不花五人領探馬赤軍。

translations.literal: Right Capital Guard: At the founding of the state, Muqali, by the Grand Ancestor's order, gathered the four appanages of Jalair, Uru, Mangγut, and Naihai, with Anchar, Bolu, Sain Nökö, Bulghai Badghur, and Kököbüqa leading the reconnaissance cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Right Capital Guard: at the dynasty's founding Muqali, by Genghis Khan's order, assembled the Jalair, Uru, Mangγut, and Naihai appanages; Anchar, Bolu, Sain Nökö, Bulghai Badghur, and Kököbüqa led the reconnaissance cavalry.

sentences.zh: 既平金，隨處鎮守。

translations.literal: After Jin was pacified, they garrisoned wherever [needed].
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin were subdued, they garrisoned wherever required.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，世祖以五投下探馬赤立蒙古探馬赤總管府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Shizu used the reconnaissance cavalry of the five appanages to establish the Mongol Reconnaissance Cavalry Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 Kublai Khan formed the Mongol Reconnaissance Cavalry Headquarters from the five appanage reconnaissance units.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，罷其軍，各於本投下應役。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan, their army was disbanded; each served duty under his own appanage.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 this force was disbanded and men returned to their appanage obligations.

sentences.zh: 十九年，仍令充軍。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, they were again ordered to serve as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 they were again conscripted for military service.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，樞密院奏，以五投下探馬赤軍俱屬之東宮，復置官屬如舊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized that the reconnaissance cavalry of the five appanages should all belong to the Eastern Palace, restoring offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 the bureau proposed placing all five appanage reconnaissance units under the heir apparent and restoring their former command structure.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改蒙古侍衛親軍指揮使司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, it was changed to the Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 it was renamed the Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，改隆福宮右都威衛使司。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, it was changed to the Longfu Palace Right Capital Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1294 it became the Longfu Palace Right Capital Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 唐兀衛：至元十八年，阿沙、阿束言：「今年春，奉命總領河西軍三千人，但其所帶虎符金牌者甚眾，征伐之重，若無官署，何以防閑之。」

translations.literal: Tangut Guard: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, Asha and Azu said: "This spring, by order I have overall command of three thousand Hexi troops, but those bearing tiger tallies and gold plaques are very numerous; for weighty campaigns, if there is no office, how can they be restrained?"
translations.idiomatic: Tangut Guard: in 1281 Asha and Azu reported: "This spring I was ordered to command three thousand Hexi troops, but many bear tiger tallies and gold plaques; for major campaigns, without a headquarters, how can they be controlled?"

sentences.zh: 樞密院以聞，遂立唐兀衛親軍都指揮使司以總之。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported this, and thereupon the Tangut Guard Personal Army Command was established to command them.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs relayed the request, and the Tangut Guard Personal Army Command was established.

sentences.zh: 貴赤衛：至元二十四年立。

translations.literal: Imperial Yellow Guard: established in the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Yellow Guard: established in 1287.

sentences.zh: 右阿速衛：至元九年，初立阿速拔都達魯花赤，後招集阿速正軍三千餘名，復選阿速揭只揭了溫怯薛丹軍七百人，扈從車駕，掌宿衛城禁，兼營潮河、蘇沽兩川屯田，並供給軍儲。

translations.literal: Right Asud Guard: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan, the Asud Badghur darughachi was first established; later more than three thousand regular Asud troops were recruited, and again seven hundred Asud Jebegun Küreg qeshig soldiers were selected to escort the imperial carriage, managing palace guard and capital security, also operating garrison farms on the Chao and Su rivers and supplying military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Right Asud Guard: in 1272 the Asud Badghur darughachi was first appointed; later over three thousand regular Asud troops and seven hundred selected Asud royal-guard qeshig soldiers were assigned to escort the emperor, guard the capital, farm along the Chao and Su rivers, and supply provisions.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，為阿速軍南攻鎮巢，殘傷者眾，遂以鎮巢七百戶屬之，並前軍總為一萬戶，隸前後二衛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, as the Asud army attacked Zhenchao in the south, the wounded were many; thereupon the seven hundred households of Zhenchao were attached to it, and together with the former army totaled ten thousand households, subordinate to the Forward and Rear Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 the Asud army suffered heavy casualties attacking Zhenchao in the south; seven hundred Zhenchao households were attached to it, bringing the combined force to ten thousand households under the forward and rear guards.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，始改立右衛阿速親軍都指揮使司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, the Right Guard Asud Personal Army Command was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 the Right Asud Personal Army Command was formally established.

sentences.zh: 左阿速衛：亦至大二年改立。

translations.literal: Left Asud Guard: also established in the second year of Zhida.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Asud Guard was likewise established in 1309.

sentences.zh: 右衛率府：延祐五年，以詹事禿滿叠兒所管速怯那兒萬戶府，及迤東、女直兩萬戶府，右翼屯田萬戶府兵，合為右衛率府，隸皇太子位下。

translations.literal: Right Guard Rate Command: In the fifth year of Yanyou, the Sükenär wanhu office managed by the Household Superintendent Tumanjir, together with the Eastern Route and Jurchen wanhu offices and the Right Wing garrison-farm wanhu troops, were combined as the Right Guard Rate Command, subordinate to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Rate Command: in 1318 the Sükenär wanhu under Household Superintendent Tumanjir, the Eastern Route and Jurchen wanhu commands, and right-wing garrison farmers were merged into the Right Guard Rate Command under the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 康禮衛：武宗至大三年，定康禮軍籍。

translations.literal: Kangli Guard: In the third year of Zhida under Wuzong, Kangli military registers were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Kangli Guard: in 1310 Wuzong fixed the Kangli military registers.

sentences.zh: 凡康禮氏之非者，皆別而黜之，驗其實，始得入籍。

translations.literal: All who were not of Kangli lineage were separated and dismissed; only after verifying their status could they enter the register.
translations.idiomatic: Non-Kangli claimants were struck from the rolls; only verified Kangli were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 及諸侯王阿只吉、火郎撒所領探馬赤，屬康禮氏者，令樞密院康禮衛遣人乘傳，往置籍焉。

translations.literal: As for reconnaissance cavalry under princes Azigi and Huolangsa belonging to the Kangli, the Bureau of Military Affairs Kangli Guard was ordered to send men by relay post to establish registers.
translations.idiomatic: Reconnaissance cavalry of princes Azigi and Huolangsa claimed by the Kangli were registered by dispatch from the Kangli Guard under the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗仁衛：至治二年，右丞相拜住奏：「先脫別鐵木叛時，沒入亦乞列思人一百戶，與今所收蒙古子女三千戶，清州徹匠二千戶，合為行軍五千，請立宗仁衛以統之。」

translations.literal: Zongren Guard: In the second year of Zhizhi, Right Chancellor Bayan memorialized: "When Töge Temür rebelled earlier, one hundred households of Yiqilieis people were confiscated; together with three thousand Mongol children and women now collected, and two thousand craftsmen of Qingzhou, totaling five thousand marching troops—please establish the Zongren Guard to command them."
translations.idiomatic: Zongren Guard: in 1322 Chancellor Bayan proposed: "When Töge Temür rebelled, one hundred Yiqilieis households were confiscated; with three thousand Mongol dependents now gathered and two thousand Qingzhou artisans, five thousand marching troops should form a Zongren Guard."

sentences.zh: 於是命右丞相拜住總衛事，給降虎符牌面，如右衛率府，又置行軍千戶所隸焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Right Chancellor Bayan was ordered to oversee guard affairs; tiger tally plaques were issued as for the Right Guard Rate Command, and marching-thousandhousehold offices were also established subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was appointed to command the guard, issued tiger tallies like the Right Guard Rate Command, and subordinate marching-thousandhousehold offices were created.

sentences.zh: 右欽察衛：至元二十三年，依河西等衛例，立欽察衛。

translations.literal: Right Qangli Guard: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan, following the Hexi guards' precedent, the Qangli Guard was established.
translations.idiomatic: Right Qangli Guard: in 1286, following the Hexi guard precedent, the Qangli Guard was established.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，分為左右兩衛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, it was divided into left and right guards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 it was split into left and right guards.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，以本衛屬大都督府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansli, it was placed under the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1329 it was placed under the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 右翊蒙古侍衛親軍都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.

sentences.zh: 宣忠斡羅思扈衛親軍都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Loyal Oros Guard Personal Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal Oros Guard Personal Army Command.

sentences.zh: 威武阿速衛親軍都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Martial Asud Personal Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Asud Personal Army Command.

sentences.zh: 東路蒙古侍衛親軍都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Eastern Route Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Route Mongol Personal Guard Army Command.

sentences.zh: 女直侍衛親軍萬戶府。

translations.literal: Jurchen Personal Guard Army Wanhu Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen Personal Guard Army Wanhu Office.

sentences.zh: 高麗女直漢軍萬戶府管女直侍衛親軍萬戶府。

translations.literal: The Koryo-Jurchen-Han Army Wanhu Office managed the Jurchen Personal Guard Army Wanhu Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Koryo-Jurchen-Han Army Wanhu Office oversaw the Jurchen Personal Guard Wanhu Office.

sentences.zh: 鎮守海口侍衛親軍屯儲都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Haikou Garrison Personal Guard Army Garrison Storage Command.
translations.idiomatic: Haikou Garrison Personal Guard Garrison Storage Command.

sentences.zh: 宣鎮侍衛。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年四月，諭隨路管軍萬戶，有舊從萬戶三哥西征軍人，悉遣至京師充防城軍：忙古䴙軍三百一十九人，嚴萬戶軍一千三百四十五人，濟南路軍一百四十人，脫赤剌軍一百四十九人，糺查剌軍一百四十五人，馬總管軍一百四十四人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, an edict was issued to wanhu commanding troops along each route: soldiers who had formerly followed Wanhu Sange on the western campaign were all to be sent to the capital to serve as city-defense troops: three hundred nineteen Mangγut troops, one thousand three hundred forty-five troops of Yan Wanhu, one hundred forty troops of Jinan Route, one hundred forty-nine troops of Toγolcha, one hundred forty-five troops of Jochal, one hundred forty-four troops of Commander Ma.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1260 Kublai Khan ordered route commanders: troops who had followed Wanhu Sange on the western campaign were to report to the capital as city-defense forces—319 Mangγut soldiers, 1,345 under Yan Wanhu, 140 from Jinan Route, 149 under Toγolcha, 145 under Jochal, and 144 under Commander Ma.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，諭益都大小管軍官及軍人等：「先李鋋懷逆，蒙蔽朝廷恩命，驅駕爾等以為己惠，爾等雖有效過功勞，殊無聞報，一旦泯絕，此非爾等不忠之愆，實李鋋懷逆之罪也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, an edict was issued to the great and small military officials and soldiers of Yidu: "Formerly Li Tan harbored rebellion, obscuring the court's gracious command, driving you to serve as his private benefit; although you had meritorious achievements, there was especially no report of reward—once extinguished, this was not your disloyalty's fault, but truly Li Tan's crime of harboring rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1262 the emperor addressed Yidu's military officers and troops: "Li Tan once rebelled and hid the court's favor, driving you to fight for his private ends; though you earned merit, he never rewarded you. His fall was not your disloyalty but Li Tan's treason.

sentences.zh: 今侍衛親軍都指揮使董文炳來奏其詳，言爾等各有願為朝廷出力之語，此復見爾等存忠之久也。

translations.literal: Now the Personal Guard Army Commander-in-Chief Dong Wenbing has come to memorialize the details, saying that you each have words of wishing to exert strength for the court—this again shows your long-standing preservation of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Dong Wenbing now reports that you have pledged renewed loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今命董文炳仍為山東東路經略使，收集爾等，直隸朝廷，充武衛軍近侍勾當。

translations.literal: Now Dong Wenbing is ordered to remain Eastern Route Pacification Commissioner, to gather you and be directly subordinate to the court, serving as Martial Guard troops for close attendance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenbing is reappointed Eastern Route Pacification Commissioner to gather you under direct court authority as Martial Guard for palace service.

sentences.zh: 比及應職，且當守把南邊，堤防外隙，庶內境軍民各得安業。

translations.literal: Before taking up regular duties, for the time being you shall guard the southern frontier and defend against external gaps, so that military and civilians within the interior may each secure their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Until regular assignment, you are to hold the southern frontier so civilians inland may live in peace.

sentences.zh: 爾等宜益盡心，以圖勛效。」

translations.literal: You should increasingly exert your hearts to plan meritorious achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Serve with all your heart and win merit."

sentences.zh: 至元二年十二月，增侍衛親軍一萬人，內選女直軍三千，高麗軍三千，阿海三千，益都路一千。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Personal Guard Army was increased by ten thousand men: within it three thousand Jurchen troops, three thousand Koryo troops, three thousand Ahai troops, and one thousand Yidu Route troops were selected.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1265 the personal guard was expanded by ten thousand men—three thousand Jurchen, three thousand Koryo, three thousand Ahai, and one thousand from Yidu Route.

sentences.zh: 每千人置千戶一員，百人置百戶一員，以領之。

translations.literal: For each thousand men a chiliarch was established; for each hundred men a centurion was established to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Each thousand had a chiliarch; each hundred a centurion.

sentences.zh: 仍選丁力壯銳者，以應役焉。

translations.literal: Still the strong and sharp in physical strength were selected to answer service.
translations.idiomatic: The fittest men were chosen for active duty.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，帝謂樞密臣曰：「侍衛親軍，非朕命不得發充夫役。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, the emperor said to Bureau of Military Affairs officials: "The Personal Guard Army may not be sent to fill corvée labor except by Our command.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1266 the emperor told the Bureau of Military Affairs: "Personal guard troops may not be assigned corvée labor without my order.

sentences.zh: 修瓊華島士卒，即日放還。」

translations.literal: The soldiers repairing Qionghua Island are to be released and sent home that same day."
translations.idiomatic: The troops working on Qionghua Island were to be released and sent home at once."

sentences.zh: 四年七月，諭東京等路宣撫司，命於所管戶內，以十等為率，於從上第三等戶，簽選侍衛親軍一千八百名。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, an edict was issued to the Pacification Commission of the Eastern Capital and other routes, ordering that within households under their jurisdiction, at a rate of ten grades, from the third grade upward households, one thousand eight hundred Personal Guard soldiers were to be selected by lot.
translations.idiomatic: In July 1267 the Eastern Capital pacification commission was ordered to draft 1,800 personal guard soldiers from households ranked third grade or higher on the ten-grade scale.

sentences.zh: 若第三等戶不敷，於第二等戶內簽補。

translations.literal: If third-grade households were insufficient, selection was to be supplemented from second-grade households.
translations.idiomatic: If third-grade households could not supply enough men, second-grade households were to fill the quota.

sentences.zh: 仍定立千戶、百戶、牌子頭，並其家屬同來，赴中都應役。

translations.literal: Still chiliarchs, centurions, and squad leaders were fixed, and their families came together to proceed to the Central Capital for service.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliarchs, centurions, and squad leaders were appointed, and families accompanied the men to the capital for duty.

sentences.zh: 十四年五月，以蒙古軍與漢軍相參，備都城內外及萬壽山宿衛，仍以也速不花領圍宿事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year, Mongol and Han troops were mixed to prepare palace guard inside and outside the capital and at Wanshou Mountain; Yisubuhua was still appointed to lead encampment guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1277 Mongol and Han troops were combined to guard the capital, its outskirts, and Wanshou Mountain, with Yisubuhua continuing to command encampment guard.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，總管胡翔請還侍衛軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, Commander Hu Xiang requested the return of guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1278 Commander Hu Xiang petitioned for the return of guard soldiers.

sentences.zh: 先是，宿州蘄縣等萬戶府士卒百人，有旨俾充侍衛軍，後從僉省嚴忠範征西川，既而嘉定、重慶、夔府皆下，忠範回軍，留西道。

translations.literal: Earlier, by edict the hundred soldiers of the Su and Qi counties wanhu office had been ordered to serve as guard troops; later they followed Vice Commissioner Yan Zhongfan on the western Sichuan campaign; after Jiading, Chongqing, and Kuizhou prefectures were taken, Zhongfan returned his army but remained in the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a hundred men from the Su and Qi wanhu office had been assigned as guards, then followed Yan Zhongfan into Sichuan; after Jiading, Chongqing, and Kuizhou fell, Zhongfan withdrew but stayed in the west.

sentences.zh: 翔上言，從之。

translations.literal: Xiang memorialized above, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiang's request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九月，以總管張子良所匿軍二千二百三十二人，充侍衛軍士。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the two thousand two hundred thirty-two men concealed by Commander Zhang Ziliang were made guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In September 2,232 soldiers hidden by Commander Zhang Ziliang were enrolled as guards.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，選揚州省新附軍二萬人，充侍衛親軍，並其妻子，遷赴京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year, twenty thousand newly submitted troops of Yangzhou Province were selected as Personal Guard soldiers, with their wives and children, and moved to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1279 twenty thousand newly submitted troops from Yangzhou, with families, were enrolled as personal guards and relocated to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十四年十月，總帥汪惟和選麾下銳卒一千人，請擇昆弟中一人統之，以備侍衛，從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-fourth year, Commander Wang Weihe selected one thousand elite soldiers under his command and requested that one of his brothers be chosen to command them for guard preparation; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1287 Commander Wang Weihe selected 1,000 elite troops and asked that a brother command them as guards; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞四年八月，詔：「蒙古侍衛所管探馬赤軍人子弟，投充諸王位下身役者，悉遵世祖成憲，發還元役充軍。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Yuanzhen under Chengzong, an edict said: "Sons and younger brothers of reconnaissance cavalry under the Mongol Guard who had entered princely household service—all are to follow Shizu's established statutes and be sent back to their original duties as soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: In August 1300 Chengzong ordered sons of Mongol Guard reconnaissance cavalry serving princes returned to military duty under Kublai's regulations.

sentences.zh: 大德六年二月，調蒙古侍衛等軍一萬人，往官山住夏。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Dade, ten thousand men of the Mongol Guard and other troops were transferred to spend summer at Guanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1302 ten thousand Mongol guard and other troops were sent to summer quarters at Guanshan.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐六年九月，知樞密院事塔失鐵木兒言：「諸漢人不得點圍宿軍士，圖籍系軍數者，雖御史亦不得預知，此國制也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yanyou under Renzong, Bureau of Military Affairs chief Tash Temür said: "Han people may not select encampment guard soldiers; even censors may not learn beforehand the registers listing troop numbers—this is a national institution.
translations.idiomatic: In September 1319 Chief Tash Temür of the Bureau of Military Affairs stated: "Han officials may not select encampment guards, and even censors may not see troop registers in advance—this is national law.

sentences.zh: 比者，領圍宿官言，中書命司計李處恭巡視守倉庫軍卒，有曠役者則罪之，以懲其後，使無怠而已。

translations.literal: Recently the encampment guard officer said the Secretariat ordered Auditor Li Chugong to inspect warehouse-guard soldiers; if any were absent from duty they were to be punished, to warn those after and keep them from slackness—that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the encampment commander reported the Secretariat had sent Li Chugong to inspect warehouse guards and punish absentees as a deterrent.

sentences.zh: 而李司計擅取軍數，箠士卒，在法為過。

translations.literal: Yet Auditor Li on his own took troop registers and flogged soldiers—in law this is an offense.
translations.idiomatic: But Li had seized troop rolls and beaten soldiers, which was itself unlawful.

sentences.zh: 臣等議，宜自中書與樞密遣人案之，驗實以聞。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discuss that the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs should jointly send men to investigate, verify the facts, and report."
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs jointly investigate and report."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，以紅城中都威衛系掌軍務之司，屬徽政院不便，命遵舊制，俾樞密總之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, because the Red City Central Capital Guard, as an office managing military affairs, was inconveniently subordinate to the Imperial Household Directorate, an order followed the old system and had the Bureau of Military Affairs command it overall.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1320 the Red City Central Capital Guard was returned from the Imperial Household Directorate to Bureau of Military Affairs control under the former system.

sentences.zh: △圍宿軍

translations.literal: △ Encampment Guard Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Encampment Guard Troops

sentences.zh: 世祖至元二十六年七月，命大都侍衛軍內，復起一萬人赴上都，以備圍宿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year of Zhiyuan under Shizu, within the capital Personal Guard Army, another ten thousand men were raised to proceed to Shangdu to prepare for encampment guard.
translations.idiomatic: In July 1289 Kublai Khan ordered another ten thousand capital personal guards to Shangdu for encampment duty.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞二年十月，樞密院臣言：「昔大朝會時，皇城外皆無墻垣，故用軍環繞，以備圍宿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yuanzhen under Chengzong, Bureau of Military Affairs officials said: "In former times at great court assemblies, outside the imperial city there were no walls; therefore troops were deployed in a ring for encampment guard.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1296 the bureau noted that before city walls existed, troops had encircled the palace at great assemblies.

sentences.zh: 今墻垣已成，南北西三畔皆可置軍，獨禦酒庫西，地窄不能容。

translations.literal: Now the walls are complete; on the south, north, and west three sides troops may all be posted; only west of the imperial wine store the ground is narrow and cannot hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Walls now allowed guards on three sides, but the area west of the imperial wine store was too narrow.

sentences.zh: 臣等與丞相完澤議，各城門以蒙古軍列衛，及於周橋南置戍樓，以警昏旦。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discussed with Chancellor Oljei that each city gate should be guarded by Mongol troops, and south of Zhou Bridge a watch tower should be placed to warn at dusk and dawn."
translations.idiomatic: They and Chancellor Oljei proposed Mongol guards at every gate and a watchtower south of Zhou Bridge for day-night alerts.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大四年正月，省臣等傳皇太子命，以大朝會調蒙古、漢軍三萬人備圍宿，仍遣使發山東、河北、河南、淮北諸路軍至京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Zhida under Wuzong, provincial officials transmitted the Crown Prince's order that for the great assembly thirty thousand Mongol and Han troops be mobilized for encampment guard; envoys were again sent to mobilize troops of Shandong, Hebei, Henan, and north of the Huai to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In January 1311, by the crown prince's order, 30,000 Mongol and Han troops were mobilized for encampment guard, with armies summoned from Shandong, Hebei, Henan, and north Huai.

sentences.zh: 復命都府、左右翼、右都威衛整器仗車騎。

translations.literal: Again the Capital Command, Left and Right Wings, and Right Capital Guard were ordered to ready weapons, chariots, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Command, left and right wings, and Right Capital Guard were told to prepare arms and transport.

sentences.zh: 六月，以諸侯王、駙馬等來朝，命發各衛色目、漢軍八百二十六人至上京，復命指揮使也幹不花領之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because feudal princes and imperial sons-in-law came to court, eight hundred twenty-six colored-troop and Han soldiers of each guard were ordered to Shangdu; Commander Yegenbuhua was again appointed to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1311, as princes and imperial sons-in-law arrived, 826 colored-troop and Han soldiers per guard went to Shangdu under Commander Yegenbuhua.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇慶元年六月，命衛率府軍士備圍宿，守隆福宮內外禁門。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Huangqing under Renzong, Guard Rate Command soldiers were ordered to prepare encampment guard and guard inner and outer forbidden gates of Longfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1312 Guard Rate troops were assigned encampment guard at Longfu Palace gates.

sentences.zh: 十一月，樞密院臣言：「皇太后有旨，禁掖門可嚴守衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Bureau of Military Affairs officials said: "The Empress Dowager has issued an edict that forbidden-palace gates must be strictly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: In November the bureau reported the empress dowager's order for stricter inner-palace security.

sentences.zh: 臣等議，增置百戶一員，及於欽察、貴赤、西域、唐兀、阿速等衛調軍士九十人，增守諸掖門，復命千戶一員，帥領百戶一員，備巡邏。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discuss adding one centurion, and from Qangli, Imperial Yellow, Western Regions, Tangut, and Asud guards transferring ninety soldiers to augment guard at the various side gates; again appointing one chiliarch and one centurion to lead patrol."
translations.idiomatic: They proposed adding a centurion and ninety men from Qangli, Imperial Yellow, Western Region, Tangut, and Asud guards for side gates, plus a chiliarch-led patrol.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年十月以諸侯王來朝，命圍宿軍士六千人增至一萬人；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yanyou, because feudal princes came to court, encampment guard soldiers of six thousand were increased to ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In October 1316, with princes attending court, encampment guards were raised from 6,000 to 10,000;

sentences.zh: 復命也了幹、禿魯分左右部領其事。

translations.literal: again Yeleghan and Tulu were ordered to lead left and right sections respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Yeleghan and Tulu were appointed to command the left and right sections.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔圍宿軍士，除舊有者，更增色目軍萬人，以備禁衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict on encampment guard soldiers: besides those already existing, another ten thousand colored-troop soldiers were added to prepare forbidden guard.
translations.idiomatic: In November another 10,000 colored-troop soldiers were added to the encampment guard.

sentences.zh: 十二月，樞密院臣言：「圍宿軍士不及數，其已發各衛者，地遠至不能如期，可遷刈葦草及青塔寺工役軍先備守衛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Bureau of Military Affairs officials said: "Encampment guard soldiers do not reach the quota; those already sent from each guard, because the distance is far, cannot arrive on schedule—those cutting reeds and Qingta Temple labor troops may first be moved to prepare guard.
translations.idiomatic: In December the bureau noted shortfalls: distant guards could not arrive on time, so reed-cutting and Qingta Temple labor troops should fill in.

sentences.zh: 其各衛還家軍士，亦發二萬五千人，令備車馬器械，俱會京師。」

translations.literal: Soldiers of each guard returning home were also to send twenty-five thousand men to prepare chariots, horses, and equipment, all assembling at the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Another 25,000 home-returning soldiers were to bring arms and assemble at the capital.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 六年閏八月，命知樞密院事眾嘉領圍宿，發五衛軍代羽林軍士，仍以千戶二員、百戶十員，擇士卒精銳者二百人屬之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixth year, Zhongjia, knowing military affairs, was ordered to lead encampment guard; five-guard troops replaced Forest Guard soldiers, still with two chiliarchs and ten centurions selecting two hundred elite soldiers subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: In intercalary August 1319 Zhongjia took encampment command; five-guard troops replaced Forest Guards, with 200 picked elites under two chiliarchs and ten centurions.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷二年二月，樞密院臣言：「去歲嘗奉旨，依先制調軍守把圍宿，此時各翼軍人，皆隨處出征，亦有潰散者，故不及依次調遣，止於右翼侍衛及右都威衛內，發軍一千一百二十六名以備圍宿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Tiansli under Wenzong, Bureau of Military Affairs officials said: "Last year We received an edict to follow the former system and mobilize troops to hold encampment guard; at that time soldiers of each wing were everywhere on campaign, and some had scattered; therefore they could not be dispatched in order—only from the Right Wing Guard and Right Capital Guard one thousand one hundred twenty-six men were sent for encampment guard.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1329 the bureau explained that last year's encampment mobilization had fallen short because troops were on campaign; only 1,126 men from the right wing and Right Capital Guard were available.

sentences.zh: 今歲車駕行幸，臣等議於河南、山東兩都府內，起遣未差軍士一千三名，以備扈從。」

translations.literal: This year as the imperial carriage travels, we your ministers discuss raising one thousand three men of undispatched soldiers from the Henan and Shandong capital commands to prepare escort."
translations.idiomatic: For this year's tour they proposed 1,003 undispatched soldiers from Henan and Shandong commands as escort.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，樞密臣又言：「比奉令旨，放散軍人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, military officials again said: "Recently by edict, guard soldiers were released.
translations.idiomatic: In May they reported a recent order releasing guard soldiers.

sentences.zh: 臣等議，常制以三月一日放散，六月一日赴限，今放散既遲，可令於八月一日赴限。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discuss that by regular rule release is on the first day of the third month and reporting for duty on the first day of the sixth month; now that release was late, they may report on the first day of the eighth month."
translations.idiomatic: Normally soldiers were released on March 1 and reported June 1; because release was late, reporting was set for August 1.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: △儀仗軍

translations.literal: △ Ceremonial Guard Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Ceremonial Guard Troops

sentences.zh: 世祖至元十二年十二月，上尊號、受冊，告祭天地宗廟，調左、右、中三衛軍五十人為蹕街清路軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Zhiyuan under Shizu, when the honorific title was assumed and registers received, sacrifices were announced to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples; the Left, Right, and Central three guard armies were mobilized—fifty men as street-clearing escort troops.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1275, at the assumption of the honorific title and temple sacrifices, fifty men from the left, right, and central guards served as street-clearing escort.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年十二月，上尊號，百官行朝賀禮，樞密院調軍一千人備儀仗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, when the honorific title was assumed, officials performed court congratulation rites; the Bureau of Military Affairs mobilized one thousand troops for ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1309 Wuzong's honorific ceremony used 1,000 troops as ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，上皇太后尊號，行冊寶禮，用內外儀仗軍數，及防護五色甲馬軍二百人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, when the Empress Dowager's honorific title was assumed and register-and-seal rites performed, the number of inner and outer ceremonial guard troops was used, and two hundred five-colored armored horse troops for protection.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1310 the empress dowager's investiture used full ceremonial guard plus 200 five-colored armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，合祭天地、太廟、社稷，用蹕街清道及守內外壝門軍一百八十人，命以圍宿軍為之，事畢還役。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, at the joint sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, the Grand Temple, and the Altar of Soil and Grain, one hundred eighty street-clearing and inner-outer rampart-gate guard troops were used; encampment guard troops were ordered to serve, and after the affair they returned to duty.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1311 joint sacrifices used 180 street-clearing and rampart guards drawn from encampment troops, then released.

sentences.zh: 七月，以奉迎武宗玉冊祔廟，用清路蹕街軍一百五十人，管軍千戶、百戶各一員。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, to welcome Wuzong's jade register into the temple, one hundred fifty street-clearing escort troops were used, with one chiliarch and one centurion commanding.
translations.idiomatic: In July 1311 welcoming Wuzong's jade register used 150 escort troops under a chiliarch and centurion.

sentences.zh: 九月，以祭享太廟，用蹕街清路軍一百五十人，千戶、百戶各一員。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for the Grand Temple sacrifice, one hundred fifty street-clearing troops were used, with one chiliarch and one centurion each.
translations.idiomatic: In September the Grand Temple sacrifice used 150 street-clearing troops with a chiliarch and centurion.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇慶元年三月，天壽節行禮，用內外儀仗軍一千人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Huangqing under Renzong, for the Heavenly Longevity Festival rites, one thousand inner and outer ceremonial guard troops were used.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1312 the Heavenly Longevity Festival used 1,000 ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 致和元年六月，以享太廟，用蹕街清路軍一百名，看糝盆軍一百名，管軍官千戶、百戶各一員。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhihe, for the Grand Temple sacrifice, one hundred street-clearing troops and one hundred grain-basin watch troops, with one chiliarch and one centurion each.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1328 the Grand Temple sacrifice used 100 street-clearing and 100 grain-basin guards with officers.

sentences.zh: 九月，行大禮，用擎執儀仗蒙古、漢軍一千名。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for the great rites, one thousand Mongol and Han troops bearing ceremonial implements were used.
translations.idiomatic: In September the great ceremony used 1,000 Mongol and Han troops bearing regalia.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷元年十一月，親祭太廟，內外用儀仗並五色甲馬軍一千六百五十名，仍命指揮青山及洪副使攝折沖都尉提調。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tiansli under Wenzong, at personal sacrifice to the Grand Temple, inner and outer ceremonial guard and five-colored armored horse troops totaled one thousand six hundred fifty; Commander Qingshan and Vice Commissioner Hong were appointed acting Mobile Corps Commandants to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1328 Wenzong's personal temple sacrifice used 1,650 ceremonial and armored troops under Qingshan and Vice Commissioner Hong as acting mobile-corps commandants.

sentences.zh: 二年，正旦行禮，用儀仗軍一千人。

translations.literal: In the second year, for New Year's rites, one thousand ceremonial guard troops were used.
translations.idiomatic: In 1329 New Year's rites used 1,000 ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 享太廟，用蹕街清路軍一百名，看守糝盆軍一百名，管軍千戶、百戶各一員。

translations.literal: For the Grand Temple sacrifice, one hundred street-clearing troops and one hundred grain-basin watch troops, with one chiliarch and one centurion each.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple sacrifice used 100 street-clearing and 100 grain-basin guards with officers.

sentences.zh: 天壽節行禮，用儀仗軍一千名。

translations.literal: For the Heavenly Longevity Festival rites, one thousand ceremonial guard troops were used.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Longevity Festival used 1,000 ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 皇后冊寶擎執儀仗，用軍一千二百名，軍官四員。

translations.literal: For the empress's register and seal ceremonial bearers, one thousand two hundred troops were used, with four military officers.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's investiture bearers used 1,200 troops under four officers.

sentences.zh: △扈從軍

translations.literal: △ Escort Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Escort Troops

sentences.zh: 世祖至元十七年三月，發忙古䴙、抄兒赤所領河西軍士，及阿魯黑麾下二百人，入備扈從。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan under Shizu, Mangγut and Cha'erchi's Hexi troops and two hundred men under Arugh's command were sent to enter escort preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1280 Mangγut and Cha'erchi's Hexi troops and 200 men under Arugh joined the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，太后將幸五臺，徽政院官請調軍扈從。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, as the Empress Dowager was to visit Wutai, Imperial Household Directorate officials requested troops for escort.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309, as the empress dowager planned a Wutai pilgrimage, the Imperial Household Directorate requested escort troops.

sentences.zh: 省臣議：「昔大太后嘗幸五臺，於住夏探馬赤及漢軍內，各起扈從軍三百人，今遵故事。」

translations.literal: Provincial officials discussed: "Formerly when the Grand Empress Dowager visited Wutai, from summer-quarter reconnaissance cavalry and Han troops three hundred escort soldiers each were raised; now follow the precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials cited precedent: the grand empress dowager had taken 300 escorts each from summer reconnaissance cavalry and Han troops.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，樞密院臣言：「去歲六衛漢軍內，以諸處興建工役，故用六千軍士於上都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Bureau of Military Affairs officials said: "Last year within the six guards' Han troops, because construction labor was underway everywhere, six thousand soldiers were used at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In November the bureau noted 6,000 Han guard troops had been diverted to Shangdu construction the previous year.

sentences.zh: 臣等議，來歲車駕行幸，復令騎卒六千人，備車馬器仗，與步卒二千人扈從。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discuss that for next year's imperial tour, again order six thousand mounted soldiers to prepare chariots, horses, and equipment, with two thousand foot soldiers for escort."
translations.idiomatic: For the coming tour they proposed 6,000 cavalry with equipment and 2,000 infantry escorts.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: △看守軍

translations.literal: △ Watch Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Watch Troops

sentences.zh: 世祖至元二十五年十一月，以軍守都城外倉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Zhiyuan under Shizu, troops were used to guard granaries outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1288 troops were assigned to guard granaries outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，大都城內倉敖有軍守之，城外豐閏、豐實、廣貯、通濟四倉無守者。

translations.literal: At first, granaries within the capital had troops guarding them; the four outside granaries Fengrun, Fengshi, Guangchu, and Tongji had no guards.
translations.idiomatic: Capital granaries already had guards, but the four suburban depots—Fengrun, Fengshi, Guangchu, and Tongji—did not.

sentences.zh: 至是收糧頗多，丞相桑哥以為言，乃依都城內倉例，每倉發軍五人守之。

translations.literal: By this time grain collection was quite abundant; Chancellor Sangge spoke on this, and thereupon following the capital inner granary precedent, five soldiers were sent to guard each granary.
translations.idiomatic: As harvests grew, Chancellor Sangge arranged five guards per suburban depot, matching inner-city practice.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中書省臣言：「樞密院公廨後，有倉貯糧，乞調軍五人看守。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Secretariat officials said: "Behind the Bureau of Military Affairs offices there is a granary storing grain; We request five soldiers transferred to guard it."
translations.idiomatic: In December the Secretariat requested five soldiers for the bureau's rear granary.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德四年二月，調軍五百人，於新浚河內看閘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Dade under Chengzong, five hundred troops were transferred to watch sluice gates on the newly dredged river.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1300 five hundred troops were posted to the newly dredged river sluices.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大四年六月，帝御大安閣，樞密院官奏：「嘗奉旨，令各門置軍守備。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Zhida under Wuzong, as the emperor attended the Great Peace Pavilion, Bureau of Military Affairs officials memorialized: "We once received an edict to place troops at each gate for guard.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1311, at the Great Peace Pavilion, the bureau cited an edict requiring guards at every gate.

sentences.zh: 臣等議，探馬赤軍士去其所戍地遠，卒莫能至，擬發阿速、唐兀等軍，參漢軍用之，各門置五十人。」

translations.literal: We your ministers discuss that reconnaissance cavalry soldiers are far from their garrison places and ultimately cannot arrive; We propose sending Asud, Tangut, and other troops mixed with Han troops for use, fifty men at each gate."
translations.idiomatic: Reconnaissance cavalry could not reach in time; they proposed fifty Asud, Tangut, and Han soldiers per gate instead.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: △巡邏軍

translations.literal: △ Patrol Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Patrol Troops

sentences.zh: △鎮遏軍

translations.literal: △ Restraint Troops
translations.idiomatic: △ Restraint Troops

sentences.zh: △鎮戍

translations.literal: △ Garrison Defense
translations.idiomatic: △ Garrison Defense

sentences.zh: 元初以武功定天下，四方鎮戍之兵亦重矣。

translations.literal: At the Yuan's beginning, with martial achievement the realm was settled, and troops garrisoned in the four directions were also weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan dynasty was founded by force of arms, and frontier garrisons were likewise a major concern.

sentences.zh: 然自其始而觀之，則太祖、太宗相繼以有西域、中原，而攻取之際，屯兵蓋無定向，其制殆不可考也。

translations.literal: Yet viewed from its beginning, Taizu and Taizong in succession possessed the Western Regions and the Central Plains; in the interval of attack and seizure, garrison troops had broadly no fixed direction—their system can scarcely be examined.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest era of Genghis and Ögedei Khan, armies had no fixed posting pattern and early arrangements are hard to trace.

sentences.zh: 世祖之時，海宇混一，然後命宗王將兵鎮邊僥襟喉之地，而河洛、山東據天下腹心，則以蒙古、探馬赤軍列大府以屯之。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time, within the four seas all was unified; then he ordered imperial princes to lead troops and garrison strategic frontier places, while the Yellow River region and Shandong, holding the realm's vital center, had Mongol and reconnaissance cavalry stationed in great prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai unified the realm, princes garrisoned key frontiers while Mongol and reconnaissance cavalry held the strategic heartland of the Yellow River basin and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 淮、江以南，地盡南海，則名藩列郡，又各以漢軍及新附等軍戍焉。

translations.literal: South of the Huai and Yangzi, the land reaching the southern sea—then famous fiefs and listed prefectures each also had Han troops and newly submitted troops garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Huai and Yangzi to the sea, fiefs and prefectures held Han and newly submitted garrisons.

sentences.zh: 皆世祖宏規遠略，與二三大臣之所共議，達兵機之要，審地理之宜，而足以貽謀於後世者也。

translations.literal: All were Shizu's grand design and far-reaching plan, jointly discussed with two or three great ministers, reaching the essentials of military opportunity, scrutinizing geographical fitness, and sufficient to bequeath plans to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: This was Kublai's grand strategy, devised with senior ministers who understood military geography well enough to guide later reigns.

sentences.zh: 故其後江南三行省，嘗以遷調戍兵為言，當時莫敢有變其法者，誠以祖宗成憲，不易於變更也。

translations.literal: Therefore afterward the three circuits of Jiangnan often spoke of transferring garrison troops; at the time none dared change the law—truly because the ancestors' established statutes were not easy to alter.
translations.idiomatic: Later the three Jiangnan circuits often debated troop rotation, but none dared alter ancestral statute.

sentences.zh: 然卒之承平既久，將驕卒惰，軍政不修，而天下之勢遂至於不可為，夫豈其制之不善哉，蓋法久必弊，古今之勢然也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end, after long peace, generals grew arrogant and soldiers lazy, military administration was not cultivated, and the realm's situation came to where nothing could be done—how was it that the system was not good? It is that when law lasts long it must decline; such is the tendency of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prolonged peace bred arrogant commanders and lax troops; administration decayed until the realm was beyond remedy—not because the system was flawed, but because institutions inevitably decay over time.

sentences.zh: 今故著其調兵屯守之制，而列之為鎮戍焉。

translations.literal: Now therefore their system of mobilizing troops for garrison and guard is set forth in detail and arranged as garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: Their troop deployment and garrison system is therefore recorded here under garrison defense.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年五月，詔漢軍萬戶，各於本管新舊軍內摘發軍人，備衣甲器仗，差官領赴燕京近地屯駐：萬戶史天澤一萬四百三十五人，張馬哥二百四十人，解成一千七百六十人，糺叱剌四百六十六人，斜良拔都八百九十六人，扶溝馬軍奴一百二十九人，內黃鐵木兒一百四十四人，趙奴懷四十一人，鄢陵勝都古六十五人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, an edict to Han wanhu: each was to select soldiers from old and new troops under his command, prepare clothing, armor, and weapons, and officials were to lead them to garrison near Yanjing: Wanhu Shi Tianze ten thousand four hundred thirty-five, Zhang Mage two hundred forty, Xie Cheng one thousand seven hundred sixty, Jochal four hundred sixty-six, Xieliang Badu eight hundred ninety-six, Fugou horse-army slaves one hundred twenty-nine, Neihuang Temür one hundred forty-four, Zhao Nu Huai forty-one, Yanling Shengdu Gu sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1260 Han wanhu were ordered to equip troops and garrison near Yanjing: Shi Tianze 10,435; Zhang Mage 240; Xie Cheng 1,760; Jochal 466; Xieliang Badu 896; Fugou cavalry slaves 129; Neihuang Temür 144; Zhao Nu Huai 41; Yanling Shengdu Gu 65.

sentences.zh: 十一月，命右三部尚書怯烈門、平章政事趙璧領蒙古、漢軍，於燕京近地屯駐；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Right Three Departments Minister Qieliemen and Pacification Commissioner Zhao Bi were ordered to lead Mongol and Han troops to garrison near Yanjing;
translations.idiomatic: In November Qieliemen of the Right Three Departments and Pacification Commissioner Zhao Bi led Mongol and Han troops to garrison near Yanjing;

sentences.zh: 平章塔察兒領武衛軍一萬人，屯駐北山；

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Tachar led ten thousand Martial Guard troops to garrison North Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Tachar led 10,000 Martial Guard troops to North Mountain;

sentences.zh: 漢軍、質子軍及簽到民間諸投下軍，於西京、宣德屯駐。

translations.literal: Han troops, hostage troops, and conscripted civilian troops of various appanages garrisoned at Xijing and Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Han, hostage, and conscripted appanage troops garrisoned Xijing and Xuande.

sentences.zh: 復命怯烈門為大都督，管領諸軍勾當，分達達軍為兩路，一赴宣德、德興，一赴興州。

translations.literal: Again Qieliemen was appointed Grand Commander to manage all military affairs; Dada troops were divided into two routes—one to Xuande and Dexing, one to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qieliemen became Grand Commander; Dada troops split between Xuande-Dexing and Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其諸萬戶漢軍，則令赴潮河屯守。

translations.literal: The various wanhu Han troops were ordered to proceed to garrison on the Chao River.
translations.idiomatic: Han wanhu troops were posted along the Chao River.

sentences.zh: 後復以興州達達軍合入德興、宣德，命漢軍各萬戶悉赴懷來、縉山川中屯駐。

translations.literal: Later Xingzhou Dada troops were merged into Dexing and Xuande; all Han wanhu were ordered to garrison in the mountains between Huailai and Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xingzhou Dada troops joined Dexing-Xuande garrisons, and Han wanhu moved to the Huailai-Jinyun mountains.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，詔田德實所管固安質子軍九百十六戶，及平灤州劉不裏剌所管質子軍四百戶，還元管地面屯駐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, an edict: the nine hundred sixteen hostage households of Tian Deshi's Gu'an command and four hundred hostage households of Liu Bulie of Pingluan were to return to their original territories for garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1262 Tian Deshi's 916 Gu'an hostage households and Liu Bulie's 400 Pingluan hostages returned to home territories.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，以金州軍八百隸東川統軍司，還成都，忽朗吉軍戍東川。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, eight hundred Jinzhou troops were subordinated to the Eastern Sichuan Command, returned to Chengdu, and Hulanggi troops garrisoned Eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 eight hundred Jinzhou troops joined the Eastern Sichuan command, returned to Chengdu, and Hulanggi troops garrisoned eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，以忙古帶等新舊軍一萬一千人戍建都。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Mangγudai's new and old troops of eleven thousand were garrisoned at Jiandu.
translations.idiomatic: In January 1274 Mangγudai's 11,000 new and old troops garrisoned Jiandu.

sentences.zh: 調襄陽府生券軍六百人、熟券軍四百人，由京兆府鎮戍鴨池，命金州招討使欽察部領之。

translations.literal: Six hundred raw-ticket soldiers and four hundred seasoned-ticket soldiers of Xiangyang Prefecture were transferred; the Jingzhao Circuit garrisoned Yachi Pool, ordered to be led by the Jinzhou Pacification Commissioner of the Qangli command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang furnished 600 raw-ticket and 400 seasoned-ticket soldiers; Jingzhao garrisoned Yachi Pool under the Jinzhou Qangli pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二月，調西川王安撫、楊總帥軍與火尼赤相合，與醜漢、黃兀剌同鎮守合答之城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Western Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Wang's troops and Commander Yang's troops were combined with Huonichi's, and together with Chou Han and Huang Ula garrisoned Heda city.
translations.idiomatic: In December Wang's Western Sichuan pacification force and Yang's command were merged with Huonichi's troops, joining Chou Han and Huang Ula to garrison Heda.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，詔以東川新得城寨，逼近夔府，恐南兵來侵，發鞏昌路補簽軍三千人戍之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year, an edict: because Eastern Sichuan's newly taken fortresses were near Kuizhou and feared southern troops might invade, three thousand conscript troops of Gongchang Route were sent to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1275, fearing Song incursions near new Eastern Sichuan fortresses by Kuizhou, 3,000 Gongchang conscripts were posted as garrison.

sentences.zh: 三月，海州丁安撫等來降，選五州丁壯四千人，守海州、東海。

translations.literal: In the third month, Pacification Commissioner Ding of Haizhou and others came to surrender; four thousand stalwart men of five prefectures were selected to guard Haizhou and Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In March Haizhou pacification commissioner Ding surrendered; 4,000 men from five prefectures were drafted to guard Haizhou and Donghai.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月，命別速䴙、忽別列八都兒二人為都元帥，領蒙古軍二千人、河西軍一千人，守斡端城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, Biesu and Hubielie Badur were appointed grand marshals, leading two thousand Mongol troops and one thousand Hexi troops to guard Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1276 Biesu and Hubielie Badur were made grand marshals with 2,000 Mongol and 1,000 Hexi troops for Khotan.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，分揚州行省兵於隆興府。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, Yangzhou Circuit troops were divided at Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1278 Yangzhou provincial troops were redeployed at Longxing.

sentences.zh: 初，置行省，分兵諸路調遣，江西省軍為最少，至是以南廣地闊，阻山溪之險，命鐵木兒不花領兵一萬人赴之，合元帥塔出軍，以備戰守。

translations.literal: At first when the circuit was established, troops of each route were mobilized; Jiangxi provincial troops were fewest; by this time because the southern Guang region was broad with mountain and stream hazards, Temür Buqa was ordered to lead ten thousand men there, combined with Marshal Tachu's army, to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit was created Jiangxi had the fewest troops; now Temür Buqa led 10,000 men south to join Marshal Tachu's force for the broad, rugged Guang region.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔以伯顏、阿術所調河南新簽軍三千人，還守廬州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an edict: the three thousand newly conscripted Henan troops mobilized by Bayan and Aju were returned to guard Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In April 3,000 newly conscripted Henan troops under Bayan and Aju were sent back to garrison Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，命荊湖北道宣慰使塔海調遣夔府諸軍士。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Pacification Commissioner Tahi of northern Jinghu Route was ordered to mobilize Kuizhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: In June Tahi, pacification commissioner of northern Jinghu, mobilized Kuizhou forces.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔以塔海征夔軍之還戍者，及揚州、江西舟師，悉付水軍萬戶張榮實將之，守禦江中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an edict: returning garrison troops from Tahi's Kuizhou campaign, together with Yangzhou and Jiangxi naval forces, were all entrusted to Naval Wanhu Zhang Rongshi to command and defend the river.
translations.idiomatic: In July returning Kuizhou veterans and Yangzhou-Jiangxi fleets were placed under Naval Wanhu Zhang Rongshi for river defense.

sentences.zh: 八月，命江南諸路戍卒，散歸各所屬萬戶屯戍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict: Jiangnan circuit garrison soldiers were dispersed to return to their respective wanhu for garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In August Jiangnan garrison troops were sent back to their wanhu camps.

sentences.zh: 初，渡江所得城池，發各萬戶部曲士卒以戍之，久而亡命死傷者眾，續至者多不著行伍，至是縱還各營，以備屯戍。

translations.literal: At first, cities taken after crossing the river had each wanhu's retinue soldiers garrisoned; over time deserters and casualties were many, and replacements often did not enter the rolls—by this time they were released to their camps for garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yang garrisons used wanhu retinues, but desertion and casualties left rolls incomplete; troops were now returned to home camps.

sentences.zh: 安西王相府言：「川蜀既平，城邑山寨洞穴凡八十三所，其渠州禮義城等處凡三十三所，宜以兵鎮守，餘悉撤去。」

translations.literal: The Anxi Prince's office said: "Sichuan being pacified, of cities, fortresses, mountain stockades, and caves totaling eighty-three places, the thirty-three including Quzhou's Liyi Fort and others should have troops garrisoned; the rest may all be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi prince's office reported 83 Sichuan strongpoints; 33 including Quzhou's Liyi Fort should be garrisoned, the rest withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔發東京、北京軍四百人，往戍應昌府，其應昌舊戍士卒，悉令散歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict sent four hundred Eastern and Northern Capital troops to garrison Yingchang; the former Yingchang garrison soldiers were all released to disperse home.
translations.idiomatic: In September 400 Eastern and Northern Capital troops garrisoned Yingchang, replacing the old garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一月，定軍民異屬之制，及蒙古軍屯戍之地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the system of separate military and civilian affiliation and Mongol troop garrison locations were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In November separate military-civilian jurisdiction and Mongol garrison zones were codified.

sentences.zh: 先是，以李鋋叛，分軍民為二，而異其屬，後因平江南，軍官始兼民職，遂因之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Li Tan rebelled, military and civilians were divided in two with different affiliation; later because of pacifying Jiangnan, military officers began also holding civil posts, and it continued thus.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Tan's rebellion military and civilians had been separated; pacifying Jiangnan led officers to hold civil posts as well.

sentences.zh: 凡以千戶守一郡，則率其麾下從之，百戶亦然，不便。

translations.literal: Whenever a chiliarch guarded a prefecture he led his subordinates with him, and centurions likewise—this was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliarchs and centurions had brought entire retinues to prefectural posts, which proved unwieldy.

sentences.zh: 至是，令軍民各異屬，如初制。

translations.literal: By this time, military and civilians were ordered each to have separate affiliation, as in the original system.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civilian affiliation was now separated again under the original system.

sentences.zh: 士卒以萬戶為率，擇可屯之地屯之，諸蒙古軍士，散處南北及還各奧魯者，亦皆收聚。

translations.literal: Soldiers took the wanhu as rate; suitable garrison land was chosen for encampment; Mongol soldiers scattered north and south and those returning to various ordos were also all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were organized by wanhu on suitable garrison land; scattered Mongol soldiers and ordos returnees were regrouped.

sentences.zh: 令四萬戶所領之眾屯河北，阿術二萬戶屯河南，以備調遣，餘丁定其版籍，編入行伍，俾各有所屬，遇征伐則遣之。

translations.literal: The masses led by four wanhu encamped in Hebei; Aju's twenty thousand households encamped in Henan for mobilization; remaining men had registers fixed and entered rolls so each had affiliation; when campaigns came they were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Four wanhu encamped in Hebei, Aju's 20,000 households in Henan for mobilization; other men were registered and called up for campaigns.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，命萬戶孛術魯敬，領其麾下舊有士卒守湖州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year, Wanhu Börü Jing was ordered to lead his subordinates' original soldiers to guard Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1279 Wanhu Börü Jing was ordered to guard Huzhou with his original troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，以唐、鄧、均三州士卒二百八十八人屬敬麾下，後遷戍江陵府，至是還之。

translations.literal: Earlier, two hundred eighty-eight soldiers of Tang, Deng, and Jun three prefectures had been placed under Jing's command, later transferred to garrison Jiangling—by this time they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: 288 Tang, Deng, and Jun soldiers once under Jing, later at Jiangling, were now returned to him.

sentences.zh: 四月，定上都戍卒用本路元籍軍士。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Shangdu garrison soldiers were fixed to use native-register troops of that route.
translations.idiomatic: In April Shangdu garrisons were ordered to use locally registered troops.

sentences.zh: 國制，郡邑鎮戍士卒，皆更相易置，故每歲以他郡兵戍上都，軍士罷於轉輸。

translations.literal: National institution: garrison soldiers of prefectures and counties were all mutually exchanged; therefore each year troops of other routes garrisoned Shangdu, and soldiers were exhausted by transport.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, garrison troops rotated annually, so other routes' men served at Shangdu at heavy transport cost.

sentences.zh: 至是，以上都民充軍者四千人，每歲令備鎮戍，罷他郡戍兵。

translations.literal: By this time, four thousand Shangdu men enrolled as soldiers were each year ordered to prepare garrison defense, abolishing other routes' garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Now 4,000 local Shangdu soldiers garrisoned annually, ending outside rotations.

sentences.zh: 六月，碉門、魚通及黎、雅諸處民戶，不奉國法，議以兵戍其地。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, households of Diaomen, Yutong, and Li and Ya regions did not obey national law; it was discussed to garrison troops in their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In June households in Diaomen, Yutong, and Li-Ya districts defied law; troop garrisons were proposed.

sentences.zh: 發新附軍五百人、蒙古軍一百人、漢軍四百人，往鎮戍之。

translations.literal: Five hundred new-subject troops, one hundred Mongol troops, and four hundred Han troops were sent to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: 500 new-subject, 100 Mongol, and 400 Han troops were sent to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 七月，以西川蒙古軍七千人、新附軍三千人，付皇子安西王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, seven thousand Western Sichuan Mongol troops and three thousand new-subject troops were entrusted to Prince Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In July 7,000 Western Sichuan Mongol and 3,000 new-subject troops were assigned to Prince Anxi.

sentences.zh: 命阇裏鐵木兒以戍杭州軍六百九十人赴京師，調兩淮招討小廝蒙古軍，及自北方回探馬赤軍代之。
